title: Combinatorial barycentric subdivisions are flag and their f-vectors count face chains

statement_alignment: The standard combinatorial barycentric subdivision is the order complex of the actual nonempty face poset. Both full and boundary face-set conventions are explicit. Its flagness and d-face count equal to the number of (d+1)-element strict chains are proved for every poset and finite family of actual subsets. The source's unspecified invariant is interpreted as the f-vector under order/combinatorial isomorphism, not complete classification or unchanged counts under subdivision.
formal_scope: Actual Mathlib AbstractSimplicialComplex and SimpleGraph comparability objects, chain-to-clique and two-face bridge, universal flag proof, genuine face/chain equivalence and k+1 f-vector, finite actual Set E face families ordered by inclusion, empty and whole-face boundary filters, and actual order-isomorphism face transport/count invariance. All 21 public theorem types and axioms are audited.
limitations: Explicitly combinatorial scope for bounded convex polytopes. The universal Lean theorem takes finite families of actual subsets and specializes by the standard face-poset definition; no separate Lean geometric Polytope type, barycenter coordinates, affine-independence/gluing/coverage theorem or finiteness theorem for geometric faces is advertised. Counts are not claimed to classify combinatorial type or remain unchanged under subdivision. Installed compiler and pinned dependency build caches remain trust inputs, not empty-machine/full-dependency-clean/Linux/hosted-CI/human/organizer verification.
